whyChoose.title: Why Bell Gardens Families Choose Us

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death claims to specific people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then certain other dependents or heirs. We can help clarify where your family fits before any deadline passes.

items.title: Watching the Clock
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity involve a much shorter window. Acting sooner rather than later helps preserve evidence and protect your family's rights.

items.title: Accounting for the Full Loss
items.desc: Beyond funeral costs, California law recognizes lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a family member provided. Our team can help make sure these losses aren't overlooked.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law prioritizes a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. We can review your family's specific situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: Is there a deadline to file a wrongful death claim in Bell Gardens?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a civil wrongful death claim. If a government entity, such as a city or county agency, may be involved, the deadline is much shorter, so it's important to get guidance early.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim relate to any criminal charges from the crash?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that may result from the same incident. Given that Bell Gardens crash reports show activity concentrated around Friday afternoon hours on corridors like Gage Avenue and Florence Avenue, families may be dealing with both processes at once, and we can help you understand how they interact.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing and carries no obligation.
